        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">During the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-10.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">10</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q10.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> During the mobility, your institution fosters the integration of the incoming mobile participants</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution appoints responsible person(s) to deal with practical issues (e.g. social, health, and/or psychological problems)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution should ensure there are named, visible persons who are responsible for the practical issues associated with integrating mobile students. This visibility should be ensured through introduction to this function during the Welcome / Orientation period and be detailed on the website so all mobile students can easily access this support, throughout their stay.&nbsp;</p><p>Non-academic mentoring and support arrangements should already be outlined in the Course Catalogue of the receiving HEI, in the section on general information for students, with relevant contact persons in the respective areas. Academic advisors should have close contact with the practical services which are available to incoming participants as they are often the first line of contact to the incoming student. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>
                                             </div>

                </div>
            </div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>

                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>

Haben Sie schon länger über eine berufliche Veränderung nachgedacht? Möchten Sie ein Unternehmen als Geschäftsführer in unserem Franchise leiten und dabei eine Aufgabe übernehmen, die wirtschaftlich attraktiv ist und echten Sinn stiftet? Dann könnte diese Chance für Sie passen – insbesondere, wenn Sie aus einer dieser Regionen kommen:

  • Aachen
  • Eschweiler
  • Stolberg
  • Alsdorf
  • Herzogenrath

Gebäude-Energieberatung

Die Nachfrage nach Gebäude-Energieberatung steigt stark: Kunden wollen ihre Öl- und Gaskosten senken und Immobilien zukunftssicher sanieren. Gleichzeitig fehlen vielerorts Gebäude-Energieberater – das schafft hervorragende Chancen für Quereinsteiger.

Ideal für Quereinsteiger

Sie benötigen keine umfangreichen fachlichen Voraussetzungen, um einen gebietsgeschützten Standort aufzubauen. ENERDOMO unterstützt Sie von Anfang an – auch nach der Neueröffnung.

Qualifizierung in 27 Tagen

In der hybriden ENERDOMO Akademie (Königstein/Frankfurt & Online) erhalten Quereinsteiger ein strukturiertes Einarbeitungs- und Qualifizierungsprogramm. Projektleiter, Ingenieure, Maschinenbauer, Handwerksmeister und Immobilienmakler finden bei uns einen schnellen Einstieg in alle Themen rund um die energetische Sanierung.

ENERDOMO Sanierungssprint

Ein- und Zweifamilienhäuser werden in 22 Werktagen energetisch saniert. Ein Taktplan steuert die Gewerke, die parallel arbeiten. Die Sanierungssprintkoordination übernimmt Baubegleitung, Bauzeitenplanung sowie die Koordinierung der Gewerke.

Zukunftsmarkt mit Sinn

„Grüne Jobs“ sind dabei mehr als ein Trend. Umwelt- und Energieberufe gehören zu den wichtigsten Zukunftsmärkten. ENERDOMO gibt Know-how an Existenzgründer und Quereinsteiger weiter, die Verantwortung übernehmen und etwas Eigenes aufbauen wollen.

Aufgaben

Wir helfen Immobilienbesitzern (privat und gewerblich), Fördermittel für energetische Sanierungen zu beantragen. Dazu erstellen wir einen Sanierungsfahrplan (iSFP) und unterstützen bei den baulichen Maßnahmen.

Statt die Arbeit von Architekten, Dachdeckern oder Heizungsbauern zu ersetzen, kooperieren wir eng mit ihnen.

Als Geschäftsführer und ENERDOMO-Partner übernehmen Sie dabei folgende Aufgaben:

BAULEITER:IN (NEUBAU & REVITALISIERUNG)

Einsatzgebiet: Münster (+50 km) & Düsseldorf (+100 km)

Du bringst fundierte Bauerfahrung mit und möchtest Deine Expertise dort einsetzen, wo sie Wirkung entfaltet? Dann freuen wir uns auf Dich.

Wir entwickeln Immobilien mit gesellschaftlicher Relevanz: Seniorenwohnen, Pflegeimmobilien und neue Konzepte für das Wohnen & Leben im Alter. Unser Anspruch: Wir wollen das Wohnen und Leben im Alter maßgeblich verändern.

Wir entwickeln neue Wohnformen von Tiny Living bis urbanem Wohnen – vom ländlichen Konzept für das Mittelstand bis zur gehobenen urbanen Wohnanlage. Wir bauen auf dem Land und in der Stadt, neu und im Bestand, und schaffen bezahlbare Wohnangebote mit Service und Betreuung für die Mitte der Gesellschaft.

Dafür gehen wir neue Wege und denken Prozesse und Verfahren neu: vom modularen Bauen über Standardisierung und Individualisierung bis zur Skalierung – unter Einsatz neuester Technologien.

Dafür suchen wir Dich: Bauleiter:in (m/w/d)

Eine Persönlichkeit, die die technische Verantwortung übernimmt: neue Bauweisen versteht, fundiert bewertet und auf der Baustelle umsetzt – im Neubau wie im Bestand, in einem jungen, agilen und digital arbeitenden Team.

Wir bauen zukunftsorientiert – agil, digital und effizient.

Wenn Du Bauprozesse weiterentwickeln und digitale Werkzeuge konsequent einsetzen möchtest, bist Du bei uns genau richtig.

Deine Rolle:

  • Technische Verantwortung für Neubau- und Revitalisierungsprojekte – vom ersten Spatenstich bis zur Übergabe

  • Technische Bewertung neuer Bauweisen, Systeme und Technologien – vom modularen bis zum seriellen Bauen

  • Mitwirkung an einheitlichen technischen Standards (z. B. wiederkehrende Grundrisse, Bauteile und Ausstattungen), die wir an vielen Standorten umsetzen

  • Steuerung von Ausschreibung und Bauausführung inkl. Koordination der Gewerke und Nachunternehmer

  • Technische Prüfung von Bestandsimmobilien auf bauliche Machbarkeit – als Grundlage für die Projektentwicklung

  • Sicherstellung von Qualität, Kosten und Terminen auf der Baustelle – in enger Abstimmung mit der Projektentwicklung

  • Digitale Baustelle: Bautagebuch, Mängel- und Terminmanagement – papierlos und datenbasiert

Was uns wichtig ist:

Wir suchen keinen klassischen Konzern-Bauleiter. Wir suchen Menschen mit Ambition, Gestaltungswillen und Umsetzungsstärke, die:

  • fundierte Erfahrung in Neubau und Bauen im Bestand mitbringen (Umbau, Sanierung, Revitalisierung)

  • Erfahrung mit modularem und seriellem Bauen bzw. Sanieren haben – oder dieses Thema aktiv in Projekte einbringen möchten

  • digitale Lösungen im Bau schätzen und Bauprozesse moderner, effizienter und datenbasiert gestalten wollen

  • Projekte auch in komplexen Situationen zielsicher zum Abschluss bringen

  • Entscheidungen treffen und Verantwortung übernehmen

  • sich fachlich und persönlich weiterentwickeln möchten

  • Prozesse aktiv gestalten, statt sie nur zu verwalten

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung als Bauleiter:in im Hochbau – idealerweise in Neubau und Bestand / Revitalisierung

  • Studium oder Ausbildung, z. B. als Bauingenieur, Bautechniker oder Meister

  • Erfahrung mit Neubauten ebenso wie mit komplexen Umbauten im Bestand

  • Technisches Verständnis für modulare, serielle und digitale Bauweisen – und die Fähigkeit, sie fundiert zu bewerten

As our Engineer - Data & Platforms (m/f/d), you build and run the internal data products that our investment team, Quantitative Research and AI Engineering rely on every day: the pipelines, datasets, APIs and tools that turn a large and growing pool of financial and alternative data into something investors can act on. The team is small, so you take ownership of real products early, and you get a manager and colleagues invested in your growth into investment and data-platform topics. What you will do

  • Build and improve the internal products the investment and research teams use daily: data pipelines, datasets, APIs, and tooling, on top of our lakehouse and orchestration stack.

  • Work directly with the teams you build for: take in their requests, triage and prioritise them, protect the integrity and consistency of the product, and explain features and implementation trade-offs in clear, non-technical language.

  • Design, build, and operate reliable data pipelines, ETLs and integrations that handle complex financial and alternative datasets.

  • Bring and reinforce good engineering habits in the team: automated testing at several levels, CI/CD, pull requests and code review, and clear documentation.

  • Contribute to operational excellence: observability, monitoring, data quality, and secure data handling.

  • Use agentic AI across engineering work (coding, review, testing, debugging, documentation) and help the team push these practices forward.


The experience you bring

  • 3 to 5 years of professional software or data engineering experience, building and operating systems in production.

  • Strong Python and strong SQL, with clean, readable code and a good sense for data modelling.

  • Proven engineering discipline: you write tests (unit, integration, data quality), work with CI/CD, and use pull requests and code review as a matter of course, and you can show how you helped a team adopt them.

  • Clear communication with non-engineers: you can explain what you built, why, and what it will and will not do, and you can say no constructively.

  • Hands-on use of AI across engineering functions, including frontier coding systems such as Claude Code and Codex, as a core part of how you work.

  • Genuine interest in investing, financial markets and data, and the ambition to grow into these topics.

  • Nice to have: Databricks or PySpark; data platform tooling such as orchestration (Airflow, Dagster or similar), lakehouse formats (Parquet, Delta, Iceberg) and AWS; experience with investment, financial or market data; building web frontends or APIs for internal tools; LLM systems in production.


2 reasons why you should not apply

  • You prefer fully specified tickets and no contact with users. Here the people you build for sit next to you, ask for things directly, and expect you to weigh in on what should be built and how.

  • You treat AI tooling as an occasional helper. We expect agentic AI to be a default in how you build, review, test, and ship, every day, not now and then.


Your mindset

  • You are a builder who loves to ship: pragmatic on trade-offs, careful on quality. You move fast, but fast does not mean sloppy.

  • You care about correctness, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability, and you leave codebases and teams better than you found them.

  • You are curious about how investment decisions are made and want to understand the data behind them, not just move it.

  • You see AI-powered development as a competitive advantage, not a novelty, and use agentic AI as a core part of how you work.

  • You communicate clearly on progress, trade-offs, and risk, and you own problems end-to-end.


What we offer

  • Work with petabytes of data and the most cutting-edge tools in and beyond asset management, with Day 1 ownership of challenging, varied work and a steep learning curve.

  • Become part of a unique success story in European asset management, alongside the most knowledgeable experts in the industry on one of the most consequential investment themes of the next decade.

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our AI Platform Teams

Our AI Platform teams build the infrastructure that powers Wayve’s embodied AI. We store and serve hundreds of petabytes of driving data, growing towards exabyte scale, to support model training, simulation and data pipelines across regions and clouds.

As our first dedicated Staff Software Engineer for Storage Platform, you’ll set the technical direction for how we manage, protect and serve this data. 🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Lead a hands-on, multi-quarter storage programme, from defining the problems and architecture to delivering platforms that teams adopt.

  • Build production services, controllers and infrastructure using Python, Go or a similar language, alongside Kubernetes and Terraform.

  • Partner with ML and data teams to understand access patterns, remove storage bottlenecks and reduce the time GPUs spend waiting for data.

  • Work with Security and Privacy to strengthen access controls, auditing and safe deletion of vehicle-collected data.

  • Write design documents and RFCs, align teams around shared standards, and mentor engineers as the platform and team grow.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Data ownership and governance: Give datasets clear owners, purposes and retention classes, with tagging and team-level cost attribution.

  • Safe lifecycle management: Build retention, deletion and re-tiering capabilities for Azure Blob, backed by dry runs, audit trails and recovery paths.

  • Partner with AI leads and wider marketing team to identify and prioritise cross-functional AI tools, skills and agents that reduce manual work across Marketing (briefing, reporting, budget tracking, onboarding)

  • Own workflow automation for repeatable operational tasks (PO/invoice tracking, budget reconciliation, status reporting) using AI-assisted tools where they save meaningful time

  • Act as the link between Marketing and the AI/upskilling programme: surface where the team is spending time on repetitive work, and bring back relevant tools, prompts or agents

  • Support rollout of new AI-enabled processes — documentation, quick training, troubleshooting first use

Budget, PO and invoice administration;

  • Act as a point of contact between Marketing and Accounting/Procurify for POs and invoices

  • Track budgets and support monthly reconciliations across the whole org

  • Maintain clear, current budget trackers

  • Use AI to optimise this process and remove friction

Tooling audits;

  • Run periodic audits of agencies and tools in use across marketing: what's licensed, what's actually used, overlap and gaps

  • Work with Marketing Operations team to recommend consolidation or decommissioning where tools are duplicated or underused

 

What we look for:

  • Comfortable owning team logistics and admin (bookings, catering, calendars) alongside higher-level operational work

  • Strong operational and project management instincts; comfortable bringing structure to ambiguity

  • Solid working experience with Asana (or equivalent) for cross-functional planning and reporting, not just task tracking

  • Budget/PO administration experience (any function)

  • Confident in AI use to improve workflows and productivity

 
 
 

What We Offer

  • Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk

  • Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays

  • Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex

  • Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva

  • Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen

  • Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence

  • Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus

  • Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party

  • Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones

  • Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

  • Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes

  • Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year

  • Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards

  • Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years

  • Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support

 

The Process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview - 30 mins - Virtual

  • Hiring Manager Interview - 30 mins - Virtual

  • Assessment Interview - 60 mins - IRL / Virtual

  • Country Manager Interview 30 mins - Virtual

  • Values Fit Interview - 30 mins - Virtual

     

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

      En tant que conseiller commercial itinérant indépendant, vous vendrez les solutions de paiement, de point de vente et logicielles de SumUp aux petites et moyennes entreprises de votre région. Vous identifierez vous-même vos prospects, gérerez votre portefeuille d'opportunités et accompagnerez les clients lors de leur mise en route.

      Vous devrez justifier d'une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp.

      Vos missions

      • Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes.

      • Cibler les entreprises locales générant d'importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp.

      • Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels.

      • Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat.

      • Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp.

      • Établir des relations avec les chefs d'entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits.

      • Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d'optimiser votre temps sur le terrain.

      • Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes.

      • Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux.

      • Au moins un an d'expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l'énergie, les technologies d'entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l'approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons.

      • Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs.

      Il s'agit d'une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l'activité des commerçants apportés.

      About the Role:

      Hi there! We're hiring a Public Sector Enterprise Account Executive II to join our Sales team.

      Our sales team is tenured, technically curious, and genuinely invested in doing right by the customer. We partner closely across the business, and we operate with a lot of trust: you're given real ownership over your territory, and you're expected to bring your own judgment to how you build it.

      As an Enterprise Account Executive II, you'll own the full sales cycle for a defined set of Public Sector enterprise accounts, from first conversation through negotiation and close, partnering with sales engineering, customer success, and your manager to navigate complex deals. This role matters because enterprise wins are how Camunda grows its footprint in large accounts, and how we prove the platform works at scale.

      This role gives you a book of enterprise accounts to grow and a real say in how you build your territory. You'll work complex deals with multiple stakeholders, and you'll have the support of sales engineering and customer success behind you as you build credibility and close.       What You Will Do

      • Build a territory plan that identifies Land opportunities and Expand possibilities, leveraging your extended resources such as Partners, Marketing, Inside Sales, Customer Success.

      • Build account plans that identify whitespace, map stakeholders, and set a realistic path to close.

      • Navigate multi-stakeholder buying committees, including technical, business, and economic buyers.

      • Own and execute the full sales cycle, from prospecting through negotiation and close.

      • Partner with sales engineering and customer success to build technical credibility and ensure a smooth handoff and adoption after close.

      • Represent Camunda's value to business and technical buyers, tailoring the message to what each audience actually cares about.

      • Handle tender processes with precision, observe pipeline health with discipline, manage Forecast with accuracy.

      What You Will Bring to the Role

      • Solid experience closing enterprise software deals end-to-end in DACH, with a track record across multiple full sales cycles. You know what it takes to move a deal from first meeting to signature without losing momentum.

      • Efficient balance between driving towards a customer vision and achieving short-term projects towards this horizon.

      • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with own initiative. The playbook will not provide all answers in advance!

      • Comfort navigating multi-stakeholder enterprise environments. You've worked complex deals involving IT, business, and procurement stakeholders, and you know how to keep everyone moving in the same direction.

      • Developing territory and account planning instincts, orchestrating resources efficiently. You can build a plan with some independence, not just work from a list handed to you, and you're learning to prioritize where your time actually pays off.

      • Experience navigating complex public procurement procedures - knowing and following the processes but also influencing them with initiative and creativity.

      • Comfort selling technical products. Experience with process automation, integration platforms, middleware, or similar technical software is a real advantage here, particularly in a Public Sector context, since you'll regularly be in the room with engineering and IT buyers.

      • Negotiation experience under real pressure. You know where to hold firm and where to flex, and you can explain your reasoning either way.

      • A relationship-building style that goes beyond the transaction. You've had customers start to treat you as an advisor, not just a vendor.

      Senior Thinkwise Developer

      Wil jij inhoudelijk richting geven aan een nieuwe Thinkwise-practice binnen Centric?

      Centric bouwt aan een nieuw gespecialiseerd Thinkwise-team dat organisaties helpt bij het ontwikkelen van moderne bedrijfsapplicaties en het vervangen van verouderde softwarelandschappen.

      Als Senior Thinkwise Developer speel jij hierin een sleutelrol. Je combineert diepgaande technische expertise met adviesvaardigheden en helpt klanten bij het realiseren van toekomstbestendige oplossingen. Daarnaast draag je actief bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van ons team, onze standaarden en onze werkwijze.

      Wat jij doet

      Als Senior Thinkwise Developer ben je verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen en realiseren van complexe softwareoplossingen binnen klantprojecten. Je bent sparringpartner voor klanten, consultants en architecten en bewaakt de kwaliteit van de oplossing van ontwerp tot oplevering.

      Naast je ontwikkelwerk begeleid je minder ervaren collega’s en draag je bij aan de inhoudelijke groei van de Thinkwise-practice.

      Jouw werkzaamheden

      ·      Ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van complexe Thinkwise-oplossingen.

      ·      Leiden van technische trajecten binnen klantprojecten.

      ·      Moderniseren van bestaande software- en ERP-landschappen.

      ·      Analyseren van bedrijfsprocessen, data en applicatiearchitecturen.

      ·      Ontwerpen van schaalbare datamodellen en integraties.

      . Maken van technische ontwerpkeuzes en architectuurvoorstellen.

      ·      Bewaken van kwaliteit, performance, security en onderhoudbaarheid.

      ·      Uitvoeren van code- en modelreviews.

      ·      Begeleiden en coachen van junior en medior ontwikkelaars.

      ·      Adviseren van klanten over digitalisering en softwaremodernisering.

      ·      Ontwikkelen van standaarden, templates en best practices.

      ·      Actief bijdragen aan de groei van het Thinkwise-team binnen Centric.


      Wat breng jij mee?

      ·      HBO of WO werk- en denkniveau.

      ·      Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring met Thinkwise-ontwikkeling.

      ·      Sterke kennis van SQL Server, databases en datamodellering.

      ·      Ervaring met complexe integraties en API-koppelingen.

      ·      Ervaring met softwaremodernisering en migratietrajecten.

      ·      Sterke analytische vaardigheden.

      ·      Ervaring met stakeholdermanagement en klantcontact.

      ·      Ervaring met Agile/Scrum-projecten.

      ·      Coachende en verbindende kwaliteiten.

      Mooi meegenomen

      ·      Ervaring als Lead Developer, Solution Designer of Technisch Consultant.

      ·      Kennis van Azure DevOps, CI/CD en DevOps-principes.

      ·      Ervaring met ERP-modernisering.

      ·      Kennis van security, auditability en datakwaliteit.

      ·      Ervaring met architectuurvraagstukken binnen enterprise-omgevingen.

      Dit krijg je van ons

      Bij Centric krijg je de kans om vanaf de basis mee te bouwen aan een nieuwe Thinkwise-practice met veel ruimte voor eigen initiatief en inhoudelijke invloed.

      Je kunt rekenen op:

      ·      Een uitstekend salaris passend bij jouw ervaring tussen de € 4500 en € 5700. Verdien je meer, bespreek het met ons.

      ·      Direct een vast contract.

      ·      26 vakantiedagen en 8% vakantiegeld.

      ·      Leaseauto of mobiliteitsvergoeding.

      ·      Flexibele werktijden en hybride werken.

      ·      Laptop en telefoon.

      ·      Opleidingsbudget en certificeringen.

      ·      Veel invloed op de technische richting van projecten.

      ·      Doorgroeimogelijkheden richting Lead Developer, Solution Architect of Competence Lead.

      Waarom kiezen voor Centric?

      Je stapt in op een uniek moment. Het Thinkwise-team staat aan het begin van een nieuwe groeifase. Dat betekent dat je niet alleen werkt aan uitdagende klantprojecten, maar ook daadwerkelijk invloed hebt op de manier waarop we onze dienstverlening, kennisontwikkeling en projectaanpak vormgeven.

      Voor ervaren Thinkwise-specialisten die méér willen dan alleen ontwikkelen, biedt deze rol een unieke combinatie van techniek, consultancy, coaching en ondernemerschap

      In de kern ondersteunt het Centric CIO Office de Centric-organisatie bij het realiseren van operational excellence en het krijgen van grip op haar processen. Het CIO Office bestaat momenteel uit een Enterprise Architect en een Business Architect. Met de toevoeging van de Data Architect zijn de kerndiensten van het team gedekt. Je rapporteert aan de CIO en werkt nauw samen met de managers van de afdelingen Internal IT en Business Applications die ook binnen de verantwoordelijkheid van de CIO vallen.

       

      Wat jij doet

      Je geeft richting aan de definitie en continue verbetering van beleid voor de levenscyclus van data en het gebruik van AI, in samenwerking met verschillende stakeholders over de internationale Centric locaties. Bevindingen moeten worden opgenomen in de bredere Enterprise Architecture, maar er moet ook aandacht zijn voor het in de praktijk brengen van initiatieven. Je adviseert interne stakeholders en data-eigenaren en vertaalt opkomende bedrijfsbehoeften naar actueel beleid. Met jouw ontwerp van onze data-architectuur stuur je de organisatie richting effectieve en efficiënte besluitvorming rondom data voor interne en commerciële oplossingen. 

      Wat doe je nog meer?

      • Het ontwerpen en onderhouden van enterprise data-architectuur (datamodellen, pipelines, platforms en integraties) 

      • Het definiëren en handhaven van datastandaarden, governance en kwaliteitskaders 

      • Het ondersteunen van data-eigenaren in de business, zodat hun data veilig, toegankelijk en compliant is 

      • De evolutie naar een moderne data architectuur leiden, inclusief een ondersteunend platform (zoals data lakehouse, real-time data) 

      • Het begeleiden en goedkeuren van AI-usecases en oplossingsontwerpen binnen de organisatie 

      • Het definiëren van best practices voor datapipelines, modelimplementatie en lifecycle management 

      • Het definiëren en implementeren van richtlijnen voor ethisch, verantwoord en veilig gebruik van AI-systemen 

      • Het stimuleren van experimenten en proof of concept initiatieven binnen de afdelingen Internal IT en Business Applications 

      • Het beïnvloeden zonder formele bevoegdheid in een complexe stakeholderomgeving 

      • Het communiceren van complexe technische concepten aan niet-technische en internationale stakeholders 

      • Het bijhouden van opkomende trends op het gebied van data-architectuur en AI

Coalition Technologies is seeking a reliable, detail-oriented, and highly organized Remote Office Assistant to support administrative, bookkeeping, billing, reporting, data entry, and internal operations tasks. As an Office Assistant, you will help support daily administrative operations, assist with entry-level bookkeeping, organize client documents, support internal reporting, and help maintain accurate company records. This position offers strong growth potential for the right candidate, including opportunities for advancement within the Accounting team or other departments.

  • International Health Insurance Reimbursement Program for eligible international team members
  • Device upgrade and learning reimbursement programs
  • Career development plans with clearly defined goals and rewards
  • Additional job-specific incentives and bonuses

 

Office Assistant Responsibilities

  • Answering phones and emails
  • Completing entry-level bookkeeping tasks, including recording expenses, organizing receipts, and maintaining transaction records
  • Resolving billing issues with clients and internal team members
  • Providing account access, usage reports, data analysis, and other ad hoc support for team members
  • Supporting quality assurance checks for internal and client-facing reports
  • Organizing new client contracts, creating invoices, and processing client payments
  • Contributing to internal database maintenance, upkeep, and data entry
  • Researching, ordering, and distributing company-wide gifts two to three times per year
  • Organizing company events, competitions, and special projects throughout the year
  • Facilitating company holiday calendars, time-off calendars, and schedule variation calendars

 

Required Skills and Qualifications

The ideal candidate will have:

  • Willingness to learn, grow, and collaborate with the team and company as a whole
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • High level of discretion, ethics, and trustworthiness
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Ability to support administrative, bookkeeping, billing, reporting, and data entry tasks
  • Innovative thinking and willingness to challenge existing methods when improvement is possible
  • Availability to work 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time
  • Reliable remote workspace with a fast computer, quality internet, camera, microphone, and speakers

 

Preferred Skills

  • The following experience is preferred but not required:
  • Intermediate spreadsheet skills
  • Experience with bookkeeping or financial record keeping
  • Experience with Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, QuickBooks Online, and Google Workspace
  • Experience supporting billing, invoicing, reporting, data entry, or administrative operations

 

Remote Work Environment

Coalition Technologies is a fully remote company. Our team works remotely with the support of time tracking software, structured communication, and a company culture designed to help remote team members succeed. We have supported remote team members for more than a decade and welcome qualified applicants from around the world.

 

Growth Opportunity

This position offers a strong opportunity for growth. Successful Office Assistants at Coalition Technologies have advanced quickly and earned promotions within the Accounting team and across other departments.

 

Compensation

For candidates located in California, New York, Washington, and Colorado, the starting base pay for this position ranges from $15 to $25 per hour. Compensation may vary based on factors such as experience, qualifications, skills test performance, geographic location, and seniority of the position offered. For candidates outside of California, New York, Washington, and Colorado, compensation may fall outside the listed range.

À propos de l’offre d’emploi

Vous êtes situé·e dans l'Est-du-Québec et détenez de l'expérience en affaires publiques et en communications ? Ce poste est peut-être pour vous !

À propos de nous:

La SDE est un propriétaire à but non lucratif qui conçoit, construit et gère des logements répondant aux besoins de la population de l’Est-du-Québec. Notre entreprise est un OBNL gestionnaire d’actifs immobiliers sans but lucratif offrant à sa communauté une expérience de vie axée sur le lien social. Le bien-être étant la principale préoccupation de l’entreprise, elle donne accès à des services variés d’une grande qualité et à proximité.

À propos du poste :

  • La Mission : L’organisation est à la recherche d’un(e) conseiller-ère principal-e aux affaires publiques qui jouera un rôle clé dans le positionnement et le rayonnement de la SDE
  • L'Impact : La personne sera responsable à la fois de l’élaboration de stratégies transversales de communication, de relations publiques et de relations gouvernementales et de leur mise en œuvre. Il s’agit donc d’une position névralgique exigence agilité et polyvalence.
  • L'Environnement : Une équipe dynamique et soudée de 12 personnes, horizontale et bienveillante, avec un accompagnement sur mesure pour faciliter votre intégration.

Ce que vous ferez :

  • Élaborer et exécuter le plan annuel de relations publiques afin de maximiser la couverture médiatique positive de nos projets immobiliers régionaux.
  • Bâtir et entretenir des relations de confiance proactives avec les élus municipaux, provinciaux et les MRC afin de faciliter l'acceptabilité sociale de plus de 20 nouveaux projets d'habitation par an.
  • Rédiger et produire tous les contenus stratégiques (communiqués, notes de breffage, mémoires administratifs, allocutions) avec rigueur.
  • Prendre en charge l'animation quotidienne de nos plateformes numériques (Facebook, LinkedIn) pour faire croître notre communauté.
  • Coordonner la logistique des annonces publiques, des conférences de presse et des visites de chantiers sur l'ensemble du territoire de l'Est-du-Québec.
  • Effectuer une veille médiatique et politique hebdomadaire afin de fournir des recommandations stratégiques d'action à la direction générale.

Qualifications :

  • Résider obligatoirement sur le territoire de l'Est-du-Québec et détenir un permis de conduire valide (déplacements fréquents sur le terrain).
  • Expérience de 3 à 5 ans en communications ou affaires publiques
  • Excellentes aptitudes rédactionnelles et esprit d'analyse aiguisé en français.
  • Grande autonomie, polyvalence et agilité pour piloter des dossiers de front dans un environnement en forte croissance.

Ce qui vous distingue :

  • Connaissance fine du milieu municipal québécois ou des rouages gouvernementaux.
  • Sensibilité ou expérience concrète dans le secteur de l'économie sociale ou des OBNL.
  • Aisance à communiquer en anglais pour soutenir notre expansion future hors du Québec.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre :

  • Fourchette salariale : Salaire très compétitif établi selon l'expérience, avec une fourchette de 30,75$ à 46,13$, jumelé à une structure de rémunération variable basée sur l'atteinte des résultats et une indexation annuelle.
  • Télétravail / Hybride : Formule hybride très flexible avec accès à nos bureaux de Rimouski ou de Métis-sur-Mer. Pour les candidats en Gaspésie, le poste est en télétravail, incluant des déplacements réguliers sur le terrain.
  • Avantages sociaux : Programme complet d'assurances collectives dès votre premier jour en poste et régime de REER collectif en cours d'implantation.
  • Avantages additionnels : 4 semaines de vacances annuelles après un an, 5 congés personnels mobiles utilisables dès l'embauche.Téléphone cellulaire et ordinateur portable fournis ou remboursés.
  • Horaires de travail : Flexibilité totale selon la conciliation travail-vie personnelle. Formule de travail personnalisable au choix entre 32h00 et 40h00 par semaine.
